newsitem.title: UK: LPC-Czech National Bank seeks $1 bln syndicat loan.
newsitem.headline: LPC-Czech National Bank seeks $1 bln syndicat loan.

text.p: LONDON, June 5 (LPC) - The Czech National Bank is seeking a $1 billion syndicated loan which marks the state's Euroloan market debut, bankers said.
The credit is being arranged to rebuild currency reserves, which were drained last week as the central bank struggled to support the crown against heavy downward pressure from speculative investors.
Banks are currently holding negotiations with the central bank, and have submitted bids, the bankers said.

Chase Investment Bank, Commerzbank, Deutsche, JP Morgan and SBC Warburg have been linked to the deal, although no details have been confirmed. The banks in question described the reports as premature.

The Czech National Bank is understood to be paying a margin of 10 bps over LIBOR for the one year standby facility, which at $1 billion would be the largest syndicated loan to emerge from the Czech Republic to date. The $750m facility for SPT Telecom, which was arranged by Chase and Citibank in July 1996, held the previous record.

The rumoured pricing is in line with the only other benchmark for Czech sovereign risk, the three-year $150m facility for the Czech Export Bank. That facility was arranged by JP Morgan in June 1996, and was priced at 12.5 bps over LIBOR, and was indirectly guaranteed by the state.
Bankers welcomed news of the deal sayging that it would diversify the Czech Republic's borrowing base which is dominated by financial institutions.
Last month, renewed pressure forced the central bank to float the crown which has since seen the currency fall more than ten per cent against its former dollar/mark peg. Newsroom 44-0171-542-8367
